And the life of Sarah was a hundred and twenty-seven years, the years of the life of Sarah.
And Sarah died in Kiriath-Arba (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan, and Abraham came to lament for Sarah and to weep for her.
And Abraham rose from beside his dead and spoke to the sons of Heth, saying,
"I am a resident foreigner and a settler among you. Give me a holding for a grave among you, so that I may bury my dead out of my sight."
And the sons of Heth answered Abraham, saying to him,

"Listen to us, my lord. You are a chieftain of God [alt: a mighty chieftain] among us. In the choicest of our graves bury your dead. Not a man among us will withhold his grave from you, to keep you from burying your dead."
And Abraham rose and bowed down to the people of the land, to the sons of Heth.
And he spoke with them, saying, "If you are willing for me to bury my dead out of my sight, listen to me, and appeal to Ephron son of Zohar for me,
that he may give me the cave of Machpelah, which is his, which is at the edge of his field. For silver in full let him give it to me among you as a holding for a grave."
Now Ephron was sitting among the sons of Heth, and Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the ears of the sons of Heth, of all who entered the gate of his city, saying,
"No, my lord, listen to me. The field I give to you, and the cave that is in it, to you I give it. Before the eyes of the sons of my people I give it to you. Bury your dead."
And Abraham bowed down before the people of the land.
And he spoke to Ephron in the ears of the people of the land, saying, "But if you—if only you would listen to me! I give the silver for the field. Take it from me, so that I may bury my dead there."
And Ephron answered Abraham, saying to him,
"My lord, listen to me. Land worth four hundred shekels of silver—between me and you, what is that? And bury your dead."
And Abraham listened to Ephron, and Abraham weighed out for Ephron the silver that he had spoken of in the ears of the sons of Heth, four hundred shekels of silver, current among the merchants.

And the field of Ephron that was in Machpelah, that was in front of Mamre—the field and the cave that was in it and all the trees that were in the field, that were within its whole border on every side—was made over
to Abraham as a purchase before the eyes of the sons of Heth, among all who entered the gate of his city.
And afterward Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah, facing Mamre (that is, Hebron), in the land of Canaan.
And the field and the cave that was in it were made over to Abraham as a holding for a grave, from the sons of Heth.
